title: Implementation notes - M1 public semantic kernel and reference Node
subtitle: M1-W0 timestamp remediation verified locally; independent rereview pending; W1 locked · 2026-09-07 02:01 CDT
intro: Each item is a decision, deviation, or tradeoff made during implementation. Acknowledge if fine. Discuss to write what should change. Revert to flag for undo.

groups.label: M1-W0 - close implementation decisions and freeze executable schemas

items.title: Accepted M0 source hashes are not available in the public repository

body.Spec said: Create a sanitized manifest for the exact accepted M0 decision bundle using stable decision IDs and content SHA-256 values before implementation proceeds.
body.What I did: Validated the plan guardrails and searched the current public tree plus all reachable public Git history for the accepted M0 ADR bundle or its recorded source hashes. Neither is present. I did not inspect a private repository or substitute hashes of newly reconstructed public ADRs.
body.Why: A derived or self-referential hash would not prove traceability to the exact accepted M0 sources and would weaken the plan's explicit W0 stop gate.
body.Risk: M1-W1 is not allowed to start. An operator must provide the stable M0 decision IDs and exact source SHA-256 values as sanitized inputs, without private paths or source content, before M1-W0 can resume.
body.Followup: Supply the sanitized ID-to-SHA-256 mapping for the accepted M0 decision bundle, then rerun M1-W0 from the existing clean code checkpoint.

items.title: Recovered the accepted M0 bundle from immutable Git blobs

body.Spec said: Publish a sanitized content-hash manifest for the exact accepted M0 decision bundle and make the public ADRs self-sufficient.
body.What I did: Located the accepted M0 commit, read ADRs 0001 through 0009 from its immutable Git blobs, copied those exact bytes into the public repository, and recorded only stable M0 ADR IDs, public paths, and SHA-256 values. The private working tree was not modified.
body.Why: Exact blob hashing preserves the accepted lineage even though the private working tree currently contains an unrelated user edit.
body.Risk: The local contract proves byte equality and rejects private location markers. The corrected contract passed a second independent adversarial review.

items.title: Kept M0 lineage verification at the workspace boundary

body.Spec said: Add every M1 test to the coordinator-owned Phase 4 classification and preserve engine package isolation.
body.What I did: Classified the M0 manifest and ADR byte-equivalence check as a workspace contract test rather than an engine-owned test.
body.Why: The check reads repository architecture documents that are intentionally absent from the installed engine wheel. Keeping it outside packages/engine/tests avoids making engine isolation depend on checkout-only files.
body.Risk: The lineage contract runs in the repository verification suite, not when consumers test the installed engine distribution. Runtime protocol contracts remain engine-owned.

body.Spec said: The public source manifest must identify the exact accepted bundle without publishing private locations.
body.What I did: Removed the private repository identifier from public test code, required the exact top-level manifest shape, scanned decoded JSON text, and required exactly nine ordered unique decision IDs.
body.Why: Independent adversarial review proved that raw-byte scanning missed JSON escapes and dictionary comparison could hide duplicate IDs.
body.Risk: Repository-specific denylist values must remain operator-supplied audit inputs rather than literals in public artifacts.
body.Followup: Completed: the corrected contract passed focused tests and a second independent adversarial review.

items.title: Rejected duplicate JSON keys before decoding

body.Spec said: The public manifest must reject private metadata and bind one exact decision bundle.
body.What I did: Added duplicate-key rejection through the JSON object-pairs hook for every manifest object, with a focused regression test.
body.Why: The second adversarial pass showed that standard JSON decoding silently discarded an earlier duplicate key before shape and privacy validation.
body.Risk: The manifest parser is intentionally stricter than Python's default JSON loader.

items.title: Source builds need an explicit writable Conan home

body.Spec said: Probe source and wheel installation for Python 3.12 through 3.14 on macOS ARM64 and Linux x86_64.
body.What I did: Ran all 12 cells. The first source attempt failed because Conan's default home was outside the writable sandbox. Redirecting CONAN_HOME to an isolated writable directory made the complete source matrix pass.
body.Why: sqlcipher3 source builds use Conan to compile SQLCipher and OpenSSL.
body.Risk: Source builders need Conan 2, CMake, a compiler toolchain, and a writable Conan home. The Linux x86_64 cells ran in official Python containers under Docker x86_64 emulation on Apple Silicon rather than on separate physical hardware.

items.title: Production databases use derived raw SQLCipher keys

body.Spec said: Freeze SQLCipher KDF settings and the passphrase-envelope profile before storage work.
body.What I did: Kept SQLCipher compatibility 4 and the 256,000-iteration PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 profile for password-keyed migrations, while specifying a 256-bit HKDF-derived raw database key for ordinary production opens. Kept the measured RFC 9106 memory-constrained Argon2id profile for portable root-key envelopes.
body.Why: The Brain root key already supplies high-entropy key material. Applying a password KDF during each database open adds cost without strengthening that key, while migration compatibility still needs fixed password-KDF values.
body.Risk: Later storage code must distinguish raw-key production opens from password-keyed migration opens and reject any profile mismatch.

items.title: Bounded the synthetic corpus generator after finding a retry loop

body.Spec said: Generate 256 reproducible unique exact-label-set shards without reading real Brain data.
body.What I did: Changed deterministic label selection from truncated digest bytes to a hash-ranked 64-label inventory and added a hard retry bound. The corrected generator produces 256 unique sets, including the 16-label and 50,000-record boundaries.
body.Why: The original one-label selection was biased toward the smallest byte value and could retry forever before any benchmark database was created.
body.Risk: The frozen limits are based on this synthetic distribution and must not be presented as measurements of private or real usage.

items.title: Packaged the complete public decision authority

body.Spec said: Make the public ADRs and schemas self-sufficient and update packaged resources additively.
body.What I did: Included the M0 manifest, ADRs 0001 through 0011, the protocol overview, M1 compatibility evidence, and the protocol schema and conformance trees in the applicable source or engine artifacts. The canonical Phase 4 classifier and generated reports now inventory the additions.
body.Why: A source distribution should carry the public semantic authority it references instead of depending on a repository checkout.
body.Risk: The completed Phase 4 evidence files remain byte-identical; only the coordinator-owned policy, classifier, and canonically generated reports changed.

body.Spec said: Update licenses and SBOM inputs when freezing the Node dependency set.
body.What I did: Recorded the selected direct dependency versions, license expressions, and upstream sources in compatibility evidence, refreshed the lock file, and added the dependency attribution inventory to every shipping NOTICE copy.
body.Why: The lock is the transitive SBOM input; the compatibility record and NOTICE make the direct M1 choices reviewable before release assembly changes in a later wave.
body.Risk: Release assembly must still collect exact license texts for the resolved transitive environment when it produces a future M1 candidate.

items.title: Preserved wheel isolation while installing locked native prerequisites

body.Spec said: A clean top-level wheel install must include the Reference Node dependency set without compiling native code on a supported wheel target, while the existing Phase 4 isolation checks remain intact.
body.What I did: Extended the canonical acceptance harness to export and install each artifact's locked third-party runtime requirements as wheels before installing the product wheel with --no-index. The app contract now requires the engine node extra, Starlette, and Uvicorn.
body.Why: The earlier Phase 4 harness intentionally installed product wheels with no dependency index. M1 introduces required third-party runtime dependencies, so those prerequisites must be staged explicitly without weakening product-wheel isolation.
body.Risk: The harness depends on the workspace lock export remaining synchronized with package metadata; the artifact and compatibility baselines enforce that relationship.

items.title: Full coordinator verification later passed in the managed runner

body.Spec said: Run coordinator verification after integration and preserve completed v0 and Phase 4 behavior.
body.What I did: The first run exposed a nested sandbox-exec restriction, so I preserved the unchanged product test and diagnosed the runner instead of weakening it. A later full make verify completed without deselection: Ruff passed, strict MyPy checked 566 source files, 3,322 tests passed, six Python artifacts built, and artifact policy passed.
body.Why: The later clean run supersedes the temporary runner limitation while preserving the original test and product behavior.
body.Risk: That green result covers commit f23b4ce. A later 3,337-test full verification covers the second remediation. Independent acceptance remains separate.

items.title: Initial implementation did not pass independent review

body.What happened: The execution driver reported M1-W0 complete at commit a6d92a9, but a fresh independent review found three P1, five P2, and three P3 contract or evidence gaps. The completion claim was withdrawn immediately.
body.Main gaps: Grant and receipt authority data, independently verifiable trust and transfer formats, logical purge proof, complete changes and record envelopes, usable custody ports, adversarial negative cases, typed commit results, request-binding validation, durable raw matrix receipts, and cross-shard RRF evidence.
body.Gate: M1-W1 remains locked until remediation passes the focused checks, full make verify, artifact verification, and a fresh independent rereview.

items.title: Remediating W0 at the protocol and evidence boundaries

body.What I did: Expanded the executable schema catalog, added cross-field semantic validation, replaced placeholder signatures with deterministic Ed25519 trust vectors, froze operational key-custody methods, made purge evidence prove row and FTS deletion, changed the synthetic benchmark to RRF-60, and ran a fresh reproducible 12-cell storage matrix.
body.Evidence: All 12 source and wheel cells passed on macOS ARM64 and Linux x86_64 for Python 3.12 through 3.14. The aggregate raw receipt records sanitized reproduction commands, exact probe stdout, and the hardened probe SHA-256.
body.Risk: The first remediation passed full local verification but did not pass independent rereview. W1 remains locked.

items.title: Second independent review found four remaining protocol gaps

body.What happened: The strict rereview of exact commit f23b4ce returned NOT READY with zero P0, two P1, two P2, and zero P3 findings.
body.Findings: Continuity documents disclosed a prior canonical commit digest; owner-key validity did not constrain Node certification or rotation; query pages bypassed nested evidence Brain checks; and the decryption port could not receive the full AEAD associated data.
body.What I changed: Replaced public ledger-head details with a domain-separated commitment to the complete signed prior receipt, enforced half-open owner chronology with validly signed boundary tests, recursively validated query evidence, and froze exact ciphertext, wrapped-key, decrypt, and rotation port shapes.
body.Gate: Focused verification and full make verify pass: Ruff, strict MyPy over 566 source files, 3,337 tests, six artifacts, and artifact policy are green. A fresh independent verdict remains required before W0 can close or W1 can begin.

items.title: Follow-up review exposed ambiguous submillisecond timestamps

body.What happened: The strict review of exact commit 5f1395a cleared all four preceding findings but returned NOT READY with one new P2. JSON Schema accepted arbitrary RFC 3339 fractional seconds while Python temporal comparison truncated beyond microseconds.
body.Counterexamples: Two independently generated, fully signed chains changed meaning after truncation: Node issuance appeared after owner activation when it was before, and appeared at owner retirement when it was before.
body.What I changed: Wire timestamps now accept canonical UTC Z only, with either whole seconds or exactly three millisecond digits. Schema and semantic parsing enforce the same rule, and tests reproduce both signed counterexamples.
body.Gate: Focused verification and full make verify pass: Ruff, strict MyPy over 566 source files, 3,344 tests, six artifacts, and artifact policy are green. A fresh independent rereview remains required before W0 can close or W1 can begin.
